name: Ozone Layer Crisis & Recovery
info: Human-made chemicals nearly destroyed Earth's protective ozone layer before international action halted the damage

nested.name: CFC–ozone link discovered
nested.info: Mario Molina and F. Sherwood Rowland publish paper in Nature showing CFCs destroy stratospheric ozone

nested.name: Vienna Convention adopted
nested.info: First international treaty on ozone protection; framework for future protocols

nested.name: Antarctic ozone hole discovered
nested.info: Farman, Gardiner & Shanklin publish satellite and ground data revealing massive seasonal ozone depletion over Antarctica

nested.name: Montreal Protocol signed
nested.info: Landmark treaty phasing out production of ozone-depleting substances; eventually ratified by every UN member state

nested.name: Montreal Protocol in force
nested.info: Global CFC phase-out begins; considered the most successful environmental treaty in history

nested.name: Largest ozone hole recorded
nested.info: Antarctic ozone hole reaches record 29.9 million km², roughly three times the area of the United States

nested.name: Kigali Amendment adopted
nested.info: Extends Montreal Protocol to phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), potent greenhouse gases used as CFC replacements

nested.name: Projected global ozone recovery
nested.info: Ozone layer outside polar regions expected to recover to 1980 levels

nested.name: Projected Arctic ozone recovery
nested.info: Arctic stratospheric ozone expected to return to 1980 levels

nested.name: Projected Antarctic ozone recovery
nested.info: Antarctic ozone hole expected to fully close, completing the decades-long recovery

name: Climate Change
info: The defining crisis of the modern era: rising greenhouse gas concentrations are destabilizing Earth's climate system

nested.name: Scientific Understanding
nested.info: Over a century of research establishing the science of anthropogenic climate change

nested.name: Arrhenius greenhouse calculation
nested.info: Svante Arrhenius first calculates that doubling atmospheric CO₂ would raise global temperatures by 5–6°C

nested.name: Callendar links CO₂ to warming
nested.info: Guy Stewart Callendar presents evidence that rising CO₂ from fossil fuels is warming the planet

nested.name: Keeling Curve measurements
nested.info: Charles David Keeling begins continuous CO₂ monitoring at Mauna Loa Observatory; the resulting curve becomes an icon of climate science

nested.name: First World Climate Conference
nested.info: WMO conference in Geneva issues declaration that CO₂ from fossil fuels could cause serious climate change

nested.name: Hansen testifies to US Senate
nested.info: NASA scientist James Hansen tells Congress he is 99% certain that global warming is caused by human activity

nested.name: IPCC established
nested.info: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change created by WMO and UNEP to assess climate science

nested.name: CO₂ passes 350 ppm
nested.info: Atmospheric CO₂ crosses 350 ppm, the level later identified by scientists as the safe upper limit

nested.name: IPCC First Assessment Report
nested.info: Concludes that human activities are substantially increasing greenhouse gas concentrations

nested.name: CO₂ passes 400 ppm
nested.info: Mauna Loa records daily CO₂ above 400 ppm for the first time in at least 3 million years

nested.name: Global temperature crosses +1.0°C
nested.info: Annual global mean temperature first exceeds 1.0°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline

nested.name: IPCC Sixth Assessment Report
nested.info: Most comprehensive climate assessment yet; states it is 'unequivocal' that human influence has warmed the planet

nested.name: CO₂ annual mean passes 422 ppm
nested.info: Atmospheric CO₂ continues its relentless rise at approximately 2.5 ppm per year

nested.name: +1.5°C threshold breached
nested.info: 2024 becomes the first calendar year with global mean temperature exceeding 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels

nested.name: Projected +2.0°C global warming
nested.info: Under current policies, the world is projected to cross 2.0°C of warming above pre-industrial levels

nested.name: International Agreements
nested.info: Decades of negotiations have produced binding and non-binding climate commitments — repeatedly undermined by withdrawal and inaction

nested.name: Rio Earth Summit
nested.info: UN Conference on Environment and Development opens UNFCCC for signature; 154 nations sign

nested.name: UNFCCC in force
nested.info: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change enters into force with 197 parties

nested.name: Kyoto Protocol adopted
nested.info: First treaty with binding emission reduction targets for industrialized nations; commits to 5% reduction below 1990 levels

nested.name: US rejects Kyoto Protocol
nested.info: President George W. Bush announces the US will not ratify the Kyoto Protocol, calling it 'fatally flawed'

nested.name: Kyoto Protocol in force
nested.info: Enters into force after Russian ratification; first commitment period 2008–2012, extended through 2020

nested.name: Copenhagen Accord
nested.info: COP15 ends in a non-binding political accord; widely seen as a failure of international climate diplomacy

nested.name: Paris Agreement adopted
nested.info: 196 parties agree to limit warming to well below 2°C, pursuing efforts to limit to 1.5°C above pre-industrial

nested.name: Paris Agreement in force
nested.info: Enters into force in record time; but pledged national contributions remain far short of stated goals

nested.name: US first withdrawal from Paris
nested.info: President Trump announces US withdrawal; effective November 2020. Rejoined by President Biden on January 20, 2021

nested.name: Glasgow Climate Pact
nested.info: COP26 strengthens Paris commitments; first COP decision explicitly mentioning fossil fuel phase-down

nested.name: US second withdrawal from Paris
nested.info: President Trump signs executive order withdrawing the United States from the Paris Agreement for the second time

nested.name: Extreme Weather & Wildfires
nested.info: Climate change is driving unprecedented heatwaves, wildfires, and storms with increasing frequency and intensity

nested.name: European heat wave
nested.info: Kills over 70,000 people across Europe; the deadliest natural disaster in European recorded history

nested.name: Russian heat wave
nested.info: Record temperatures up to 44°C cause wildfires and crop failure; approximately 56,000 excess deaths

nested.name: Hurricane Harvey
nested.info: Stalls over Houston delivering unprecedented 1.5 m of rainfall; $125 billion in damage

nested.name: Australian Black Summer
nested.info: Bushfires burn 18.6 million hectares, destroy 5,900 buildings, and kill an estimated 3 billion animals

nested.name: Pacific Northwest heat dome
nested.info: Lytton, British Columbia records 49.6°C — the highest temperature ever recorded in Canada; over 1,400 deaths

nested.name: Canadian wildfire season
nested.info: Worst wildfire season in Canadian history: 18.5 million hectares burned, smoke blankets eastern North America

nested.name: Sea Level Rise
nested.info: Global mean sea level has risen ~20 cm since 1900 and the rate is accelerating as ice sheets and glaciers melt

nested.name: Satellite altimetry era
nested.info: Precise satellite measurements begin; reveal sea level rising at 3.1 mm/year, accelerating to 4.5 mm/year by the 2020s

nested.name: Projected sea level +0.3–1.0 m
nested.info: IPCC projects 0.3–1.0 m of sea level rise by 2100 depending on emissions scenario; could exceed 2 m under high-end ice sheet instability

nested.name: Climate Tipping Points
nested.info: Critical Earth system thresholds that, once crossed, trigger self-reinforcing changes irreversible on human timescales

nested.name: Arctic sea ice decline
nested.info: Summer sea ice extent has declined ~40% since satellite records began in 1979; September 2012 record low of 3.41 million km²

nested.name: Projected ice-free Arctic summer
nested.info: First summer with less than 1 million km² of Arctic sea ice, exposing dark ocean that absorbs more heat

nested.name: AMOC weakening detected
nested.info: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation has weakened ~15% since the mid-20th century; full collapse would radically alter Northern Hemisphere climate

nested.name: Projected AMOC collapse risk
nested.info: Studies suggest the Atlantic circulation could collapse between the 2030s and 2090s under continued warming

nested.name: Permafrost thaw acceleration
nested.info: Arctic permafrost contains ~1,500 billion tonnes of carbon; thawing releases methane and CO₂ in a self-reinforcing feedback loop

nested.name: Greenland ice sheet mass loss
nested.info: Greenland is losing ice at an accelerating rate; complete loss would raise sea levels by 7.2 metres over millennia

nested.name: West Antarctic Ice Sheet destabilization
nested.info: Marine ice sheet instability may have been triggered; could contribute 3–5 m of sea level rise over centuries

name: Sixth Mass Extinction
info: Earth is experiencing its sixth mass extinction, the first caused by a single species; current extinction rates are 100–1,000 times the natural background rate

nested.name: Last Passenger Pigeon dies
nested.info: Martha, the last Passenger Pigeon, dies at Cincinnati Zoo; the species once numbered 3–5 billion individuals

nested.name: Last Thylacine dies
nested.info: The last known Tasmanian Tiger, Benjamin, dies at Hobart Zoo; driven to extinction by hunting, habitat loss, and disease

nested.name: Wildlife population collapse
nested.info: WWF Living Planet Index documents 69% average decline in monitored wildlife populations between 1970 and 2018

nested.name: CITES signed
nested.info: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species adopted; regulates trade in over 38,000 species

nested.name: First global coral bleaching
nested.info: El Niño–driven ocean temperatures trigger the first recognized global mass coral bleaching event

nested.name: Baiji dolphin declared extinct
nested.info: An extensive Yangtze River survey fails to find a single Baiji; the first cetacean driven to extinction by human activity

nested.name: Third global coral bleaching
nested.info: The longest and most widespread coral bleaching event on record; 75% of the world's reefs experience bleaching-level heat stress

nested.name: Insect apocalypse study published
nested.info: Krefeld study reveals 75% decline in flying insect biomass over 27 years in German protected areas

nested.name: Last male Northern White Rhino dies
nested.info: Sudan dies at Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Kenya; only two females remain, making the subspecies functionally extinct

nested.name: IPBES: 1 million species at risk
nested.info: UN global assessment finds 1 million animal and plant species threatened with extinction, many within decades

nested.name: Fourth global coral bleaching
nested.info: NOAA confirms the fourth global bleaching event in April 2024; record ocean temperatures devastate reefs worldwide

nested.name: Projected Amazon rainforest dieback
nested.info: At current deforestation rates and warming, the Amazon could cross a tipping point and transition from rainforest to savanna

name: Ocean Crises
info: The world's oceans face acidification, plastic pollution, dead zones, and ecosystem collapse on an unprecedented scale

nested.name: Ocean acidification
nested.info: Oceans have absorbed ~30% of human CO₂ emissions, dropping pH by 0.1 units — a 26% increase in acidity, faster than any change in 300 million years

nested.name: Ocean dead zones expansion
nested.info: Oxygen-depleted dead zones have quadrupled since the 1950s; over 700 identified globally by 2024, driven by nutrient runoff and warming

nested.name: Great Pacific Garbage Patch forming
nested.info: Plastic debris accumulates in the North Pacific subtropical gyre; by the 2020s it covers 1.6 million km² — three times the size of France

nested.name: Great Pacific Garbage Patch documented
nested.info: Sailor and researcher Charles Moore discovers vast concentrations of floating plastic debris while crossing the North Pacific

nested.name: Microplastics found in human blood
nested.info: Study in Environment International detects microplastic particles in 80% of human blood samples tested

nested.name: Projected: more plastic than fish
nested.info: Ellen MacArthur Foundation projects that by weight, the ocean could contain more plastic than fish if current trends continue

name: Chemical Contamination
info: Synthetic chemicals released into the environment persist for decades or centuries, accumulating in ecosystems and human bodies

nested.name: DDT Era
nested.info: A miracle pesticide that became a global ecological poison before being largely banned

nested.name: DDT's insecticidal properties discovered
nested.info: Paul Hermann Müller discovers DDT kills insects on contact; he later receives the 1948 Nobel Prize for this work

nested.name: Widespread DDT use
nested.info: DDT sprayed massively for agriculture and mosquito control; accumulates in food chains causing eggshell thinning in birds of prey

nested.name: Silent Spring published
nested.info: Rachel Carson's book documents DDT's devastating effects on wildlife; sparks the modern environmental movement

nested.name: US bans DDT
nested.info: EPA bans DDT for agricultural use in the United States; other nations follow over the next decades

nested.name: Stockholm Convention adopted
nested.info: Global treaty on persistent organic pollutants restricts DDT to disease vector control only; 152 signatories

nested.name: PFAS: Forever Chemicals
nested.info: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances do not break down in the environment and have contaminated virtually every living organism on Earth

nested.name: Teflon accidentally invented
nested.info: Roy Plunkett at DuPont accidentally discovers polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE); commercial production begins in 1945

nested.name: PFAS in mass production
nested.info: DuPont begins using PFOA (C8) to manufacture Teflon; 3M produces PFOS for Scotchgard. Both companies aware of toxicity risks by the 1960s

nested.name: PFAS contamination exposed
nested.info: Attorney Rob Bilott begins uncovering evidence that DuPont knowingly contaminated water supplies near its Parkersburg, West Virginia plant

nested.name: C8 Science Panel study
nested.info: Independent panel finds probable links between PFOA exposure and kidney cancer, testicular cancer, thyroid disease, and other conditions

nested.name: PFOA Stewardship Program
nested.info: EPA and eight major companies agree to phase out PFOA by 2015; companies switch to shorter-chain PFAS that are also persistent

nested.name: PFAS detected in rainwater globally
nested.info: Stockholm University study finds PFAS in rainwater everywhere on Earth exceeds EPA safety guidelines; nowhere on the planet is safe

nested.name: EPA proposes first PFAS drinking water limits
nested.info: EPA proposes enforceable limits of 4 parts per trillion for PFOA and PFOS in US drinking water

name: Deforestation
info: Industrial-scale destruction of the world's forests, eliminating carbon sinks and biodiversity at catastrophic rates

nested.name: Amazon deforestation
nested.info: Over 800,000 km² of Amazon rainforest cleared since 1970 — an area larger than Turkey — primarily for cattle ranching and soy

nested.name: Southeast Asian peat fires
nested.info: El Niño–fueled fires in Indonesia's peatlands burn for months; release CO₂ equivalent to 13–40% of global fossil fuel emissions that year

nested.name: Peak Amazon deforestation rate
nested.info: Annual Amazon deforestation reaches 27,772 km²; international pressure and monitoring programs lead to decline in following years

nested.name: Indonesian fires crisis
nested.info: Devastating peat and forest fires release more CO₂ daily than the entire US economy; 500,000+ cases of respiratory illness

nested.name: Global tree cover loss accelerating
nested.info: Global Forest Watch documents the loss of 437 million hectares of tree cover from 2001 to 2023 — over 10% of global forest area

name: Environmental Disasters
info: Catastrophic pollution events that killed thousands and contaminated vast areas, often spurring regulatory action decades too late

nested.name: Great Smog of London
nested.info: Coal smoke and fog blanket London for five days; kills approximately 12,000 people and sickens 100,000

nested.name: Bhopal gas disaster
nested.info: Methyl isocyanate leak at Union Carbide plant kills 3,800+ immediately; estimated 15,000–20,000 total deaths over following years

nested.name: Chernobyl disaster
nested.info: Reactor No. 4 explodes at Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant; worst nuclear disaster in history, contaminating vast areas of Europe

nested.name: Chernobyl Exclusion Zone
nested.info: 2,600 km² remains uninhabitable; will not be safe for human habitation for approximately 20,000 years

nested.name: Exxon Valdez oil spill
nested.info: Tanker runs aground in Prince William Sound, Alaska, spilling 37,000 tonnes of crude oil; devastates marine ecosystem

nested.name: Deepwater Horizon oil spill
nested.info: Largest marine oil spill in history: 4.9 million barrels flow into the Gulf of Mexico over 87 days

nested.name: Fukushima Daiichi disaster
nested.info: Earthquake and tsunami cause three reactor meltdowns; largest nuclear disaster since Chernobyl, contaminating the Pacific

name: Projected Futures Under Current Trajectory
info: What the science projects if current emission trajectories and ecological destruction continue

nested.name: Coral reefs effectively eliminated
nested.info: At +1.5°C, 70–90% of coral reefs die; at +2°C, 99% are lost, collapsing marine food webs that support 500 million people

nested.name: Climate migration acceleration
nested.info: World Bank projects 216 million internal climate migrants by 2050 across six regions due to drought, floods, and sea level rise

nested.name: Global crop yield decline
nested.info: Projected 10–25% decline in global crop yields per degree of warming; 3.5 billion people face food insecurity by mid-century

nested.name: 1 billion in unlivable heat zones
nested.info: Regions regularly exceeding wet-bulb temperatures of 35°C — the limit of human survivability — could be home to over 1 billion people

nested.name: Projected 3–6°C warming (worst case)
nested.info: Without drastic emission cuts, global temperatures could reach 3–6°C above pre-industrial levels — a transformation of Earth's climate unseen in millions of years
